story: Microsoft 365 Copilot – your copilot for work
text: the TaxGPT example in the GPT-4 Developer Livestream [1] was powerful. I'm hoping (soon?) for a Microsoft 365 assistant that can do the same trick on ALL your MS cloud data (docs/files/mails/notes...) Edit : the included "Business Chat" goes in the same direction (on what they call the Microsoft Graph) Also, there were interesting "coding" examples in the same livestream. So the coming GPT-4 (and 5) integration in the Power Platform [2] could be a game-changer for less technical staff. [1] [VIDEO] [2] [LINK]

If passing the bar exam, writing code alongside a human and incorporating their feedback [1], or creating a website from a crude sketch [2] aren't akin to human intelligence, then what is? At some point, you have to go from saying it's just a parlor trick to considering that maybe we're just a parlor trick as well. [1] [VIDEO] [2] [VIDEO]

story: GPT4 is up to 6 times more expensive than GPT3.5
text: Maybe it's something else ? I am genuinely not sure what they mean, this is the timecode in the announcement: [VIDEO] It seems to say that they use Be my eyes "to make the product better", so it could be humans in the loop during captioning, or maybe they are using volunteers data from Be my eyes as training set ? Or it's completely opposite, and that Be my eyes is using the OpenAI APIs ? My guess is that it is both ?

story: Robots Have Been About to Take All the Jobs for 100 Years
text: In one of GPT4's release demos, it is shown being fed a photograph of a hand-drawn web page. It then image analyses that, works out that it's a picture of a web page and turns it into a working web page ( [VIDEO] ). So here's the thing; what in that list of non-codegen tasks is more complicated than that which GPT can already automate?

story: I trusted an LLM, now I'm on day 4 of an afternoon project
text: Minor correction: GPT-4 was announced on March 14, 2023, less than two years ago.
